record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: Determine whether there exists a real almost-CL-space that is not a CL-space.

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Is there any real almost-CL-space which is not a CL-space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space with closed unit ball $B_X$ and unit sphere $S_X$. A nonempty convex subset $F \subseteq S_X$ is called a maximal convex subset of $S_X$ if it is maximal (with respect to inclusion) among the convex subsets of $S_X$. The space $X$ is called a CL-space if 
$$B_X = \operatorname{aconv}(F)$$
for every maximal convex subset $F$ of $S_X$, where $\operatorname{aconv}(F)$ denotes the absolutely convex hull of $F$ (the convex hull of $F \cup (-F)$). The space $X$ is called an almost-CL-space if 
$$B_X = \overline{\operatorname{aconv}(F)}$$
for every maximal convex subset $F$ of $S_X$, i.e., the closed absolutely convex hull of every maximal convex subset of $S_X$ equals $B_X$.

Every CL-space is an almost-CL-space. Determine whether there exists a real almost-CL-space that is not a CL-space.
artifact.category_tag: CL-spaces and numerical index of Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not produce evidence that the question of whether every real almost-CL-space is a CL-space has been settled. The problem is listed as an open problem in the survey on numerical indices of Banach spaces, and follow-up literature (e.g., on lush spaces and the Mazur–Ulam property of almost-CL-spaces) continues to treat the two classes as a priori distinct, without resolving the real case. The current status appears unverifiable from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Historical Introduction: A Walk on the Results for Banach Spaces with Numerical Index 1
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces CL-spaces (Fullerton, 1960) and almost-CL-spaces (Lima), with the latter defined via closed absolutely convex hulls of maximal convex subsets of the unit sphere.
status_evidence.claim: Almost-CL-spaces and CL-spaces are distinct definitions in the literature; the question of separating them in the real case is treated as open.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Mazur–Ulam property of almost-CL-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the class of almost-CL-spaces separately from CL-spaces, without identifying them in the real case.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to consider almost-CL-spaces as a strictly broader class to investigate, without resolving whether real almost-CL-spaces must be CL-spaces.
